page.title: FootyNet: football players and clubs find each other
page.description: Public FootyNet landing page in English and Croatian. Players build a profile and apply to club positions; clubs post positions, review applicants and message them. Every media frame holds FootyNet's own interface built in HTML and CSS with clearly labelled example data, because no photography is available. Signed-in visitors are sent to their dashboard.

architecture.contract: This page helps amateur and semi-professional football players, and the club staff recruiting them, understand what FootyNet does for their role and decide to register. The business outcome is new verified player and club accounts. Primary conversion: Register, with Sign in as the secondary action.
architecture.grid: 12-column grid. Landing content runs to 1200px; the hero and footer run to 1440px with 40px side gutters, 24px on mobile. Desktop gutters 24px. Spacing on a 4px base using 8/12/16/24/32/48/96/128.
architecture.signatureRule: From the karo hero (1505x1045): a narrow text rail at about 17% of the width sits beside one dominant media field at about 74%, and text never sits on top of the media. Every media frame on the page holds FootyNet's real interface on a deep pitch-green ground with a visible example-data tag, so the product itself is the imagery.
architecture.rhythm: Light hero with a dark-green media field, light three-step players band, dark club cards, light bento preview, light feature split, deep pitch-green trust panel, dark role split, light FAQ, deep pitch-green closing CTA, near-black footer. Section padding 80-112px on desktop and 64-80px on mobile. Never more than two dark sections in a row.

navigationDesign.layout: Follows the karo-template-01-hero left rail (reference 1505x1045), where the rail spans x 40-290px (17% width) with the wordmark at the top, grouped links from about 58% down, and a full-width button at the bottom of the first viewport. FootyNet keeps that order: wordmark, h1 statement, a 'Players' group (For players, Features), a 'Clubs' group (For clubs, FAQ), a 'Language' group (Hrvatski / English), then the Sign in text link and the full-width emerald-700 Register button. The rail belongs to the hero and is not a sticky sidebar. Once the hero leaves the viewport a 64px white top bar with a 1px slate-200 bottom border shows the wordmark, the four anchors, Sign in and Register. Repair from the DOM audit: the wordmark link and every rail and top-bar anchor get block padding and min-height so the rendered hit area is at least 44px tall while the 15px type and the reference's rail rhythm are unchanged.
behavior: Anchor links scroll natively to #players, #clubs, #features and #faq with scroll-margin-top 80px
The compact top bar appears once an IntersectionObserver on the hero reports it has left the viewport; it fades in and slides 8px down over 200ms, and no ancestor of the fixed bar carries a transform
Active anchor: emerald-800 text with a 2px emerald-700 underline; hover moves to emerald-700 over 150ms on fine pointers only

The mobile menu button (lucide Menu, 44px target) opens a full-height sheet with the same groups and the Register button; Escape or the close button dismiss it, focus is trapped while open and returns to the menu button
The language switch uses the existing next-intl flow and keeps the current anchor

transformation.compact: Under 768px, as in the karo mobile reference (783x2009): a 64px bar with the wordmark left and the hamburger right, then the h1 statement at full width, then Register full width and the Sign in link. Link groups move into the menu sheet; nothing is dropped.
transformation.medium: 768-1199px: the rail narrows to 220px and the media field takes the rest. Link groups stay visible and the language group joins the bottom row beside Sign in.
transformation.expanded: 1200px and up: the reference rail at 17% width with the statement at the top, groups from about 58% down and Register at the bottom of the first viewport.

sections.layout: Composition map from the desktop reference (1505x1045). Two columns: text rail x 2.7%-19.3%, media field x 22%-96%, so the media is about 3.2x the rail width. The h1 sits at the top of the rail, y 5%-19%, as 5 lines of Outfit 500 at 19-20px, line-height 1.3, matching the reference's small statement scale rather than a giant headline. The media field holds two frames stacked with a 20px gap and radius 0, as in the reference: frame 1 at y 3.5%-63.5% (16:9) on a #052E22 ground with the pitch-pattern markings (first of three uses), holding the hero_job_board_panel; frame 2 starts below and runs past the fold on the same green without the pattern, holding the hero_applicant_panel. Each white vignette card sits right of centre at about 62% of the frame width, matching the reference's right-weighted media mass. A white/70% example-data tag sits in the lower-left corner of each frame. Nothing overlaps the rail. Mobile reference (783x2009): a 64px bar, the statement as 3 lines at 20px with 24px margins, Register and Sign in, then a caption block above each frame (title 18px Outfit 600 plus a muted meta line), mirroring the reference's 'Coast / 2025, Aarhus' captions. Mobile frames are full width at about 1.17:1 and the inner card fills 88%.

motion.behavior: The rail wordmark, statement, link groups and Register rise 16px and fade with an 80ms stagger. Each frame fades its green ground while its white vignette card lifts 20px. The three job rows then fade in at 70ms intervals with opacity only, so no transform nests inside the card's own entrance. Frame 2 follows frame 1 by 120ms. Frames keep fixed aspect ratios so nothing shifts.
motion.reducedMotion: Every hero element renders in its final state immediately, with no transforms.

transformation.compact: One column in source order: bar, statement, Register and Sign in, then captioned frame 1 and captioned frame 2. All three job rows and all three applicants stay visible, and the actions sit above the first frame.
transformation.medium: 220px rail beside the media field; frame 2 shows its top 40% above the fold.

sections.purpose: Show club staff the four-step recruiting process, including admin approval.
sections.userQuestion: As a club, how do I find players and what has to happen first?
evidence: app/pending-approval and components/admin/PendingClubsTable.tsx (clubs are approved by admins)

copy.heading: How clubs recruit on FootyNet
body: Get approved: register your club and an admin checks it before your first ad goes live.
Post a position: describe the role, league, city and when you need the player.
Review applicants: see each player's profile, career history and availability in one list.
Message players: invite the right players to talk and arrange a trial.
Clubs are approved before they can post, so players only see checked teams.

sections.layout: Composition map from the creatiie desktop reference (1505x1045): a centred brand label at the top, then one dominant white media card held upright in the middle with smaller tilted cards flanking it, each card carrying a title, a short description and a labelled meta grid. FootyNet keeps that centre-dominant arrangement on the #03140F ground, with the reference's tilt reduced to 0 degrees because the inner content is readable interface rather than photography; that deviation is recorded here. Top row y 4%-8%: the 'For clubs' eyebrow at 13px Inter 500 sentence case centred, with 'Steps 1-4' at the right edge. Centre card x 29%-71%, y 11%-88%: a white 16px-radius card with shadow-lift holding the club_step_ui_cards vignette for the current step (Get approved), its 40px Outfit 600 title at the top left, a 2-line description, and a 2x2 meta grid reading Status / In review and Checked by / FootyNet admin, exactly mirroring the reference's Client / Year / Project type grid. Flanking cards x 3%-27% and x 73%-97%, y 20%-70%, at about 0.78:1: smaller white cards for Post a position and Review applicants, each with a title, one line and its own vignette, at 88% scale so the centre card stays dominant. The fourth step, Message players, sits as a fourth card that enters the flank row at expanded width; at medium and compact it joins the stack in order. Below the group, y 90%-96%: the closing sentence left and the emerald-300 'Register your club' link right, with a white/50% example-data tag beneath. Mobile reference (793x1716): the centre card first at full width, then each flanking card full width in step order, then the closing sentence and link.

motion.behavior: The centre card is observed first: it fades and rises 20px while its vignette scales from 0.96 to 1. The flanking cards then fade and slide 20px inward from their own sides, left then right, 80ms apart, with total stagger capped at 240ms. The meta grid rows fade 100ms after their card. Hover on a card brightens its border to white/25% over 180ms on fine pointers; step text is never hover-only.
motion.reducedMotion: Cards, vignettes and meta grids render in place and hover changes only border colour.

transformation.compact: All four cards stack full width at 4:5 in step order 1-4, each keeping its title, description, meta grid and vignette. The closing sentence and link follow the last card, aligned left.
transformation.medium: Centre card at 56% with one flanking card either side; the fourth card drops to a full-width row beneath, keeping the same order.

sections.purpose: Answer the remaining questions on eligibility, approval, cost, languages, messaging, availability and mobile use without promising anything unverified.
sections.userQuestion: What else do I need to know before I register?

copy.heading: Questions before kick-off.
body: Short answers about joining, club approval and how FootyNet works.
Who can join as a player? Any amateur or semi-professional player looking for a club. You create an account, confirm your email and complete your profile.
How do clubs get approved? A club registers, then a FootyNet admin reviews the account. Until it is approved, the club sees a pending screen and cannot post job ads.
What does it cost? Registration does not ask for any payment details. You sign up with your email, a password and your profile.
Which languages can I use? FootyNet is available in Croatian and English. Switch at any time from the menu.
How do I talk to a club? Once you have applied, the club can message you and you reply in your FootyNet inbox. You also get an email when a new message arrives.
Can I change my availability? Yes. Update it on your profile whenever your situation changes, and clubs see the new status straight away.
Can I use FootyNet on my phone? Yes. FootyNet works in the browser on phones, tablets and computers, so you can reply to a club from the training ground.
STILL HAVE A QUESTION?

The accordion spans x 14%-86% (72%) from y 27%: 7 rows, each a 1px slate-200 bordered box with 12px radius, 8px apart and 72px tall closed. Each row carries a 48px slate-100 circle with an emerald-800 lucide icon (UserRound, ShieldCheck, Wallet, Languages, MessageCircle, CalendarCheck, Smartphone), the question in Outfit 500 at 24px, and a lucide Plus/Minus at the right in emerald-800. The first row is open by default with its answer in 16px Inter slate-600 over at most 3 lines, indented to the question. Below the list: a centred 'STILL HAVE A QUESTION?' micro-label between two 48px rules, then a pill Register button (emerald-700 fill, white text, lucide ArrowRight). Mobile reference (951x1656): the heading centred over 3 lines at 48px with the second line in emerald-800, a 3-line intro, rows without the icon circle and with a 40px circular chevron button at the right, a 1px rule between question and answer in the open row, and the centred footer rule below.
